output.summary: Large coniferous tree endemic to Australia, naturally concentrated in southeast Queensland with two very small isolated populations in the northeast. It has a distinctive egg-shaped crown, very large cones and rigid, sharp-tipped leaves. Its edible nuts are eaten raw, cooked, ground into paste or bread, or traditionally creek-fermented by Indigenous Australians; shoots are also eaten.
output.edibilityNote: Indigenous Australians eat nuts raw, cooked, immature, as paste or bread, and traditionally creek-fermented; shoots are also eaten.
